systems.title: World & discovery
systems.summary: A landscape of dormant musical potential.
systems.role: Gives expansion destinations: resource sites and undiscovered instrument beings.
accepted: Top-down, radial, pathless arena around a stationary conductor.
The fiction can be strange: amorphous musical beings, perhaps living notes.
Discovery does not fix a being’s eventual placement.
questions: Are resource sites and sleeping beings separate discoveries, sometimes co-located?
What reveals new territory?

systems.title: Mining & production
systems.role: The separate-mining proposal: invest in production that funds growth and creates locations worth defending.
accepted: The idle incremental economy and purchased upgrades remain central.
Earlier direction put gathering structures at resource sites and allowed safe offline production.
questions: Keep mining as a distinct system, or source income from the orchestra?
Does production require proximity to the conductor pulse?
What does the output represent and what does it buy?

systems.title: Income & spending
systems.role: Keeps a spendable balance and turns production into decisions about growth, defense and active power.
accepted: Income and upgrades remain part of the idle incremental game.
Every ordinary conductor tap earns income; timing cannot gate that base income.
Paid rebuilding preserves musical development within the current run.
questions: One run currency or distinct spending pools?
Which upgrades improve production versus combat?
How do costs scale and what survives defeat?

systems.title: Recruitment & inventory
systems.summary: Discover a being; make it available.
systems.role: Owns which musical beings are available, independently of where they are placed or how they develop.
accepted: Recruitment, arrangement and musical development are distinct.
A discovered being can be placed away from where it was found.
questions: Inventory was proposed as the home for recruited beings: how is availability limited?
What does awakening require?
Does the collection persist after defeat?

systems.title: Arrangement & pulse
systems.role: Owns placement, proximity connections, and relationships among active instruments.
accepted: Nearby entities carry the conductor’s pulse farther through proximity.
Instrument placement is free rather than fixed to discovery sites.
questions: Which entities relay the pulse and how far?
What happens to instruments and producers beyond a destroyed relay?
What exactly does an isolated, uncoordinated instrument do?

systems.title: Musical development
systems.summary: Develop the voice, retain its identity.
systems.role: Changes how an existing instrument performs and fights; remains distinct from adding another being.
accepted: An instrument does not upgrade into a different instrument.
Acoustic and electric identities are parallel possibilities.
Development may use rhythm, phase, pitch, register, harmony, dynamics and articulation.
questions: Which changes belong to an instrument, the arrangement, the conductor, or the whole orchestra?
Which developments are purchased, chosen during runs, or permanent?

systems.title: Conductor & touch
systems.role: Owns player interventions. Conductor taps strike enemies directly and support instruments; neither passes through the automatic orchestra.
accepted: Taps directly attack and damage enemies, as well as earn income.
Supporting the orchestra (accenting an instrument) is a separate use of the same touch.
Tap, swipe, hold and voice are conductor inputs.
The conductor is stationary at the center and is the protected object.
questions: How does one tap choose between striking an enemy and supporting a nearby instrument?
What constrains attack rate and other powers?
How do active upgrades stay valuable beside growing automation?

systems.title: Automatic defense
systems.role: Resolves the orchestra’s automatic attacks, damage to instruments, destruction and rebuilding. Conductor attacks are resolved by the conductor, not here.
accepted: Instrument towers defend automatically and their attacks create music.
Instruments and structures can be damaged or destroyed.
Rebuilding preserves development during the current run.
questions: What are the instrument roles and enemy matchups?
What damage and repair rules keep losses recoverable?
Do performers sound when no valid enemy target exists?

systems.title: Enemies & crises
systems.role: Provides threats that test the growing base, arrangement and conductor.
accepted: Enemies approach from all directions.
Ordinary play can be enjoyed without constant input.
Crises benefit substantially from live conductor support.
Runs escalate until defeat.
questions: How are waves started and paced?
What makes a crisis distinct from an ordinary wave?
What happens when the player leaves during a crisis?

systems.title: Shared musical system
systems.summary: One beat; many voices and roles.
systems.role: Provides the global beat and makes gathering, conducting and instrument actions part of one musical world.
accepted: A shared global beat anchors economy and instrument actions.
Music can be intentionally dense and maximalist.
The music comes from gameplay, including instrument attacks.
questions: How is harmony maintained while voices change?
Which events create sound, and which only change future performance?
How do large numerical upgrades remain audible without endless speed or density?

systems.title: Offline progression
systems.role: Accounts for time away without simulating destructive combat.
accepted: Offline time may advance production.
Offline time cannot advance danger or destroy the orchestra.
questions: What production rate and cap apply while away?
Does awakening also advance offline?
How does a paused crisis resume?

systems.title: Run & permanent growth
systems.role: Separates one escalating performance from the player’s longer progression.
accepted: Runs escalate until the conductor falls.
Permanent progression may unlock possibilities.
questions: Do roster, base, currency and techniques persist or reset?
How does idle compounding coexist with meaningful run variation?
What exactly is recovered after defeat?

edges.label: Resource sites
edges.trigger: The pulse reaches a site of dormant musical potential.
edges.effect: A producer can be placed on that site.
questions: What reveals new territory?

edges.label: Discover beings
edges.trigger: The pulse reaches a sleeping musical being.
edges.effect: Awakening it makes the being available to recruit.
questions: Are resource sites and sleeping beings separate discoveries?

edges.label: Passive production
edges.trigger: A producer completes its division of the global beat.
edges.effect: Resonance is added to the balance, including while away.
edges.evidence: Prototype 03: mines pay out on the beat.

edges.label: Production upgrades
edges.trigger: The player spends on a producer.
edges.effect: That producer yields more per payout.

edges.label: Purchase upgrades
edges.trigger: The player spends on an instrument’s technique.
edges.effect: The instrument develops without becoming another instrument.
edges.evidence: Prototype 03: mastery, subdivision and octave doubling.

edges.label: Pay to rebuild
edges.trigger: An instrument has been destroyed.
edges.effect: Spending returns it with its musical development intact for this run. Every rebuild is Resonance not spent on growth, so recovery competes with upgrades.
questions: How does rebuild cost scale, and is return instant or delayed?
Does a recent loss discount repair, or does it cost the same whenever?
edges.evidence: Prototype 03: rebuilding costs 40% of what was invested in the structure.

edges.label: Develop powers
edges.trigger: The player spends on the conductor.
edges.effect: Touch yield or conductor powers improve.
edges.evidence: Prototype 03: touch development raises tap income.

edges.label: Available beings → placement
edges.trigger: The player places a recruited being.
edges.effect: It joins the active orchestra at a chosen position.

edges.label: Origin of the pulse
edges.trigger: Always, on the global beat.
edges.effect: The conductor’s pulse spreads outward through nearby entities.
questions: Which entities relay the pulse, and how far?

edges.label: Active orchestra
edges.trigger: An instrument is placed and connected.
edges.effect: It attacks automatically from its position.

edges.label: Performance changes
edges.trigger: An instrument develops.
edges.effect: Its attacks change: cadence, reach or strength.
edges.evidence: Prototype 03: subdivision changes attack cadence; octave doubling adds damage.

edges.label: Direct tap attacks
edges.trigger: The player taps an enemy.
edges.effect: The conductor damages it directly, without an instrument between them.
questions: How are enemies targeted by touch?
What limits attack rate?
edges.evidence: Not yet in Prototype 03: its taps earn income and accent structures but never damage enemies.

edges.label: Support: accent an instrument
edges.trigger: The player taps near an instrument and has enough conductor power.
edges.effect: That instrument’s next attacks carry the accent. This is support, separate from direct attacks.
questions: Is support the same tap aimed differently, or a different gesture?
edges.evidence: Prototype 03: aimed taps spend conductor power to accent a structure.

edges.label: Tap income
edges.trigger: Any ordinary tap.
edges.effect: Earns Resonance. Timing may add a capped bonus, but income never depends on timing.
edges.evidence: Prototype 03: every tap earns; a near-beat tap earns one capped bonus per beat.

edges.label: Targets and pressure
edges.trigger: Enemies reach the orchestra.
edges.effect: They are targeted, and they damage or destroy instruments.

edges.label: Protect producers
edges.trigger: Enemies approach a producer.
edges.effect: Nearby instruments defend the base’s income.

edges.label: Attacks sound; losses fall silent
edges.trigger: An instrument attacks, or is destroyed.
edges.effect: Its attack is a note. A destroyed instrument’s voice is absent until it is rebuilt.
questions: Do performers sound when no valid target exists?
edges.evidence: Prototype 03: a destroyed structure falls silent until rebuilt.

edges.label: Destruction breaks the pulse
edges.trigger: A destroyed instrument was relaying the pulse.
edges.effect: Recommendation: entities beyond it keep acting but lose coordination. Rebuilding or rerouting reconnects them.
questions: What does lost coordination sound and look like?
Does a gap cut off everything beyond it, or only weaken it?

edges.label: Pulse reaches producers
edges.trigger: A producer is connected, or is disconnected.
edges.effect: Recommendation: a disconnected producer slows but keeps its stored income; reconnecting restores its rate.
questions: Does connection enable production, or only improve it?

edges.label: Development changes the sound
edges.trigger: An instrument develops.
edges.effect: The change is audible: subdivision changes its rhythm, octave doubling adds pitches in the same voice.
questions: Which pitch, harmony, phase and articulation changes replace the small shared set?
edges.evidence: Prototype 03: subdivision and octave doubling are audible.

edges.label: Placement shapes the music
edges.trigger: Instruments are placed near one another or apart.
edges.effect: Undecided: whether position affects entrances, register, doubling or harmony.
questions: Does placement change the sound, or only the defense?

edges.label: Shared beat
edges.trigger: Each division of the global beat.
edges.effect: Producers pay out on the beat.

edges.label: Shared beat
edges.trigger: Each division of the global beat.
edges.effect: Instruments attack on their division of the beat.

edges.label: Time-away production
edges.trigger: The player leaves.
edges.effect: Producers keep producing.
questions: What rate and cap apply while away?
edges.evidence: Prototype 03: mines settle away time on return.

edges.label: Danger waits
edges.trigger: The player leaves.
edges.effect: Enemies do not advance and nothing is destroyed.
questions: How does a paused crisis resume?
edges.evidence: Prototype 03: away time advances mining without advancing danger.

edges.label: Defeat ends performance
edges.trigger: The conductor falls.
edges.effect: The run ends.

edges.label: Persistence boundary
edges.trigger: A new run begins.
edges.effect: Undecided: whether the roster carries over.

edges.label: Reset boundary
edges.trigger: A new run begins.
edges.effect: Undecided: whether currency, base or upgrades carry over.

edges.label: Alternative: performance income
edges.trigger: The orchestra plays.
edges.effect: Earlier alternative: playing produces income instead of separate mining.

map.title: Create a musical incremental orchestra-defense game for Android

defense.title: Define the orchestra-defense and radial-base domain

steps.title: Extend the pulse
steps.text: You place a being between the conductor and a second resource site. It relays the pulse, and a producer on the site comes online.

steps.title: The outpost produces
steps.text: The new producer pays out on the global beat. Income rises, and there is now a place worth protecting.

steps.title: An enemy breaks through
steps.text: The relay instrument is destroyed. Its voice drops out of the music immediately.

steps.title: The pulse breaks
steps.text: Everything beyond the gap is cut off. The recommendation: those instruments keep acting but lose coordination, and the producer slows but keeps its stored income.
steps.ask: Is that what should happen when an outpost loses the pulse?

steps.title: The conductor answers
steps.text: Taps strike the attacker directly, with no instrument involved. The same touches keep earning, and an aimed tap can accent a surviving instrument.

steps.title: Rebuild, or grow?
steps.text: One balance, three claims. Rebuilding returns the relay with its development intact and reconnects the outpost. The same Resonance could buy development or production instead.
